title: Seen, Heard & Supported: Creating pathways for NEET young people (not in employment, education or training)
summary_en: About the project We are looking for experienced and motivated youth organisations to join our upcoming Erasmus+ Youth Worker Mobility Study Visit exploring how we can better engage, understand and support young people who are not currently in education, employment or training (NEET). Through intercultural learning, discussion, reflection and practical activities, participants will have the opportunity to challenge assumptions, develop greater awareness of different perspectives and explore how we can create more inclusive spaces for young people. We are particularly interested in organisations with experience working directly with NEET young people and a commitment to meaningful youth participation and inclusion. Objectives The project will bring together youth workers from different European countries to: Explore what it means to be seen, heard and supported Explore culture, identity and diversity and how these shape our experiences Develop awareness of unconscious bias and how it can influence the way we see and interact with others Share experiences and good practice in working with NEET young people Possible Partners We are particularly interested in organisations that work directly with young people with fewer opportunities, including organisations that work with: Young people from ethnic minority communities. Young people involved in or leaving the criminal justice system. Young people in care or care leavers. Young people facing social, economic or educational barriers. We are looking for organisations that: Have experience working directly with these young people. Are willing to share their experiences, good practices, activities and practical tools with international partners, in a world cafe activity during the study visit Have regular activities with young people in your organisation Are interested in developing long-term parternerships. Can share real stories of impact-what has worked, what hasn't and what approaches have made a meaningful difference fo
audience: Austria, Belgium - DE, Belgium - FL, Belgium - FR, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Iceland, Ireland, Latvia, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland

title: Circus for all - Building Inclusive Communities
summary_en: About the Training Course How can youth workers create spaces where every young person feels welcome, valued, and actively involved? "TC Circus for All" is a 5-day international training course in Slovenia that empowers youth workers, volunteers, and NGO leaders to build inclusive environments where every young person feels valued. Through a practical, hands-on approach, the program combines brief theoretical discussions with active workshops in circus pedagogy, community art, and team dynamics. The course will explore how circus pedagogy, youth work and community work can support inclusion, participation, personal development. Through experiential learning and practical workshops, participants will discover innovative methods that can be adapted to different youth work contexts and to the needs of diverse groups of young people. Objectives The Training Course aims to: Strengthen competences in inclusive youth work. Explore circus pedagogy as a non-formal educational methodology. Develop practical tools for fostering participation and belonging. Exchange good practices among youth organizations from different countries. Promote creativity, cooperation, and intercultural learning. Encourage future Erasmus+ cooperation and partnership development. Methodology The Training Course will be based on non-formal education and experiential learning principles. Methods will include: Circus pedagogy workshops Cooperative games and team challenges Reflection and peer-learning sessions Community-based activities Group work and facilitated discussions Exchange of practices and project development No previous circus experience is required. Participant Profile We are looking for: Youth workers Youth leaders Volunteers NGO staff members Community workers Facilitators and trainers working with young people Participants should: Be 18+ years old. publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: Virtual Exchange - DevelopMENs
summary_en: DevelopMENS (developmens.eu) is a transnational project that brings together a consortium of partners from six countries: Italy (L’ORMA), Croatia (Vere Montis), Bulgaria (BSDA), Bosnia and Herzegovina (BRAVO), Albania (New Vision), and Kosovo (Heimerer College). This collaborative youth initiative aims to foster the personal and social development of young people through a structured, research-based educational approach. The project integrates four key areas: Self-Determination Theory (SDT) Critical Thinking Media Literacy Soft Skills Development The main objective of DevelopMENS is to promote young people’s intrinsic motivation, personal growth and social development by combining these educational components. A key outcome of the project is the DevelopMENS online learning platform, which is free and accessible to everyone. During this webinar, we will introduce the platform, present its educational contents and guide you through how to use it. Whether you are a trainer, educator, youth worker or young person, you will discover how to access the courses and resources and how to introduce the platform to other young people who may benefit from this free learning opportunity. The webinar will also provide a space for participants from different backgrounds and countries to connect, learn together, exchange experiences and share good practices related to youth personal and social development. When: 15 October 2026, 16:00–17:00 CET Where: Online via Zoom Registration form: https://zfrmz.eu/BQjZoa9oQFIksT1xErfB The session will include: Welcome & Icebreakers Introduction to the DevelopMENS MOOC and practical guidance on how to use the platform Exchange of experiences and good practices Q&A
audience: Erasmus+ Youth Programme countries , Partner Countries Neighbouring the EU

publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: Embodied Belonging
summary_en: Activity Description Embodied Belonging is an experiential Erasmus+ training course held in the quiet winter landscape of Latvia, designed to offer youth workers, trainers, and educators transformative tools rooted in eco-somatics, movement, and nature connection. When the outer world freezes into white silence, this course invites us to turn inward—exploring how belonging can be felt as a grounded, inner state of being within our own skin. By integrating body awareness, nervous system regulation, and outdoor immersion into non-formal education, participants will learn how to support both themselves and young people in feeling more connected, present, and resilient. Target Audience & Non-Formal Learning Context This training is specifically tailored for 28 participants working in non-formal learning and youth work (youth workers, trainers, facilitators, space holders, and educators aged 22+) who interact directly with young people, including those working with marginalized or disadvantaged youth. The program bridges personal practice and professional youth work methodology. Participants will gain practical, experiential NFE methods to bring fresh creativity, somatic grounding, and nature-based tools back to their local youth work practices. Main Themes & Methodology Eco-Somatics & Nervous System Regulation: Body-based tools to support youth mental health, emotional grounding, and self-care. Relational Awareness & Communication: Nonviolent Communication (NVC), consent practices, Playfight, and empathetic sharing circles. Movement & Creative Expression: Contact-inspired movement, dance jams, and sensory exercises. Nature Immersions: Silent walks, winter hiking, and forest bathing in snow-covered pine forests. Project Phases & Commitment Selected participants commit to all three project phases: Preparation: Pre-departure orientation and self-assessment. 10-Day Training Mobility: Full participation in Latvia (January 18–29, 2027). summary_en: Cohesive Youth Work – Austria Cohesive Youth Work (CYW) is an Erasmus+ international training course designed for professionals and volunteers active in non-formal education and youth work. The project brings together participants from Austria, Italy, Portugal, Romania, Hungary, and Slovakia to explore how youth work can build trust, dialogue, participation, and community cohesion. This is one complete learning journey, meaning selected participants commit to all project phases: Phase 1 – Tulln an der Donau (26–31 October 2026) Develop a strong understanding of community cohesion, conflict, power, inclusion, and dialogue through interactive non-formal learning methods, simulations, discussions, and peer exchange. Integration Phase (November 2026 – February 2027) Apply what you learn in your own community by identifying local needs and strengths, participating in online mentoring, and preparing your own community initiative. Phase 2 – Vienna (22–27 February 2027) Transform your ideas into action by learning participatory project design, stakeholder engagement, and practical tools to develop a local Cohesion Action for your community. After the training, participants will implement a small local initiative that promotes dialogue, cooperation, and youth participation. Who should apply? We are looking for 5 participants who: are 18+ and currently live in Austria or Slovakia ; are actively involved in youth work or non-formal education (NGOs, youth centres, schools, municipalities, community initiatives, volunteering, etc.); have a good command of English; are motivated to participate in both training courses and implement a local follow-up activity. We particularly encourage applications from youth workers, volunteers, educators, and community leaders from rural and smaller municipalities across Austria. publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: Training of Trainers on Being Civically Engaged
summary_en: NGO Awero team, Nexes Interculturals, Cities of Learning Network partners, and the International Youth Work Trainers Guild are offering a 6th modular training for trainers, aligned to the European Training Strategy (ETS) competence model. The training course will contribute to the development of the ETS trainers’ competences in the area of “Being Civically Engaged”. Understanding and asserting the trainer's work as an act of civic engagement Connecting relevant [youth] policies and educational programmes to own values, beliefs and different political perspectives Reflecting on personal civic engagement, values and beliefs, and integrating them in the training practice in a responsible and constructive way Supporting learners in developing critical thinking and using the diversity of opinions and beliefs as a source of learning Applying democracy and human rights principles in the design and delivery of training activities. Programme of the training course The programme opens with introductions, setting the learning stage, and exploring participants' personal values and beliefs, then links these to trainer identity and active citizenship. Midweek, the group will travel to Barcelona to explore civic engagement and local training practices, including a Migrantour optional session in one of Barcelona’s neighbourhoods. The later days shift to developing pilot civically engaged training practice ideas, examining diversity, democracy and human rights as sources of learning, and covering resources for trainers' professional development and recognition. Please check the draft programme attached to this call for participants. Highlights of this training activity: Aligned to the ETS competence model for Trainers, the course objectives and content are aligned with professional competences expected for Facilitating Learning in international training settings in the field of youth work. Certified training - the broad coalition of partners will create opportunities for the course

publishing_authority_code: Others
title: Synapse: Connecting Networks for Impact
summary_en: This Partnership Building Activity (PBA) consists of four days of interactive sessions and local visits where participants will have the opportunity to exchange good practices and strengthen networks with like-minded associations and organizations active in the Erasmus+ program. The idea is to gather organizations that want to expand their actions and implement new projects. There will be a balance between newcomer organizations and more experienced ones, in order to share proven methodologies, navigate common challenges, and foster peer-to-peer mentorship. Inspired by the concept of neural connectivity, this activity treats each organization as a key node in a dynamic European network. Just as neurons build stronger pathways through interaction, our aim is to spark active collaboration, combine fresh perspectives with proven experience, and turn creative synergies into real results. Over these four days, participants will focus specifically on forging strategic connections to co-create Erasmus+ Key Action 2 (KA2) partnerships in the Youth and Adult Education fields—leaving with concrete project ideas, trusted consortiums, and clear roadmaps for upcoming calls.
audience: Erasmus+ Youth Programme countries

publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: The Edge Within
summary_en: The Edge Within is an Erasmus+ Training Course for youth workers, trainers, facilitators, educators, community leaders and others actively involved — professionally or voluntarily — in youth work and non-formal learning. Many of us support young people in navigating change, uncertainty, relationships and questions of identity — while meeting similar edges within ourselves. The Edge Within is an invitation to turn some of that attention inward. For one week, 25 participants from Czechia, Latvia, Romania, Italy and Estonia will step away from their everyday routines and gather at an old Scout base surrounded by forests in Nejdek, Czech Republic. Together, we will explore the “edges” within ourselves: our patterns, reactions, boundaries, strengths and the places where we meet uncertainty, discomfort or the not-yet-known. And we will ask how greater awareness of these processes can influence the way we listen, facilitate, hold space and accompany young people. The training combines personal exploration with professional reflection. Through experiential and non-formal learning, nature-based and embodied practices, storytelling, creative expression, movement, reflection, peer learning and community living, participants will first experience the methods themselves — and then explore how they can be meaningfully and ethically adapted to their own youth work. We are looking for people who are curious, open to reflection and willing to participate fully in an experiential learning process. You do not need to be an experienced trainer or have previous experience with nature-based approaches. The setting itself will be part of the journey. We will live simply and closely together, spend meaningful time outdoors and experience November in the Czech countryside as it comes. Programme: 5–11 November 2026 Arrival: 4 November | Departure: 12 November Place: Nejdek, Czech Republic Participants: 5 from each participating country (Czechi Republic, Latvia, Romania, Italy & Estonia) Acco
audience: Czech Republic, Estonia, Italy, Latvia, Romania

title: Dive in. Foundations of conflict transformation at the interpersonal level
summary_en: What if conflict wasn’t a problem to solve, but a language to understand? This project invites you to decode the hidden messages within tension and disagreement, finding paths that lead not just to resolution, but to transformation. By engaging with the roots of conflict and exploring its role in our lives and communities, we’ll explore how it can be a catalyst for creativity, growth, and resilience. This isn’t about avoiding difficulty, it’s about diving into it and reimagining the possibilities on the other side. In a world marked by growing complexity, the need for conflict transformation has never been more urgent. This project invites participants to take a step back, return to the fundamentals, and rediscover the power of dialogue and understanding. Are you ready to shape a new narrative? Aim: To equip 25 youth workers, youth leaders and activists with tools to transform conflicts into opportunities for dialogue and growth, fostering collaboration and building inclusive communities capable of addressing challenges. Objectives - To gain a better understanding of the concepts of Peace, diverse forms of violence, conflict, non-violence and culture of peace. - To understand the importance of nonviolent conflict transformation, the variety of strategies to approach conflict and its links to the context of human rights. - To empower participants to participate and build healthy and peaceful communities and interpersonal relations. - To develop skills in emotional literacy and non-violent communication. - To map and analyse the conflicts affecting the participants in their local context. - To facilitate the process of designing at least 6 follow-up activities aiming to transform local conflicts by using conflict transformation tools. - To create a recommendations document including the framework of competencies for youth leaders to build sustainable communities and teams. Profile of participants - Youth workers, leaders, and activists interested in conflict transform

title: Mastering Digital Tools in Non- Formal Education
summary_en: This project brings together youth workers to explore how digital tools can enhance non-formal education and youth work. Through practical activities, experimentation and peer learning, participants will discover and test digital tools and methods that can make learning more interactive, creative and engaging. A particular focus will be placed on digital gamification as a way to increase young people’s motivation, participation and engagement in learning activities. Objectives of the training course: 1. Develop youth workers’ digital competences. 2. Explore digital tools and methods for non-formal education. 3. Explore digital gamification as a way to increase young people’s engagement and motivation. 4. Increase confidence in designing interactive and creative digital activities. 5. Exchange good practices and ideas between youth workers. About the coordinator organisation: Le Lab Lisieux Normandie is a secular and apolitical association, created in 2018, with the ambition of being an incubator of citizen initiatives, federating young people from Lisieux and its agglomeration, Lisieux Normandie, around European values, encouraging them to international mobility, notably through the Erasmus+ program. Profile of participants: 1. Be a legal resident of one of the partnering organisations' countries in this project. 2. Youth workers with fewer opportunities are welcome. 3. Motivated and able to take part in the full duration of the activity (training course) and be involved in the local activity in their home country (presenting a one-hour workshop with at least 10 local youths together with the country group) after the training course. 4. Having background experience in non-formal education. 5. Aged 18+. 6. Able to communicate independently in English. 7. We highly recommend keeping the gender balance. 8. title: PACT Online Conference
summary_en: Join the PACT Final Online Conference: Empowering Youth Work through PFA & Creative Techniques Over the past two years, partners across 8 countries have built, tested, and implemented an integrated framework combining psychological first aid, art-based practices, and psychoeducation to strengthen youth mental health support. We're inviting youth workers, psychologists, educators, art therapists, NGO representatives, stakeholders, and young people to join us as we close the project and share what we've built together. What you'll gain: Access to the PFA Manual — core principles and guidelines adapted for youth workers The Creative Toolkit — a practical guide to applying creative techniques in psychological first aid Entry to the PACT Interactive E-learning Platform — open-access tools and self-paced modules Real-world testimonials from practitioners who took part in international mobilities and local workshops A full overview of the project's 2-year impact, from Training of Trainers to national workshops across partner countries Date: 19 October Time: 17:00 CET Format: Online (Zoom) — access link sent to registered participants ahead of the event Language: English ❗️ Registration: https://forms.gle/24AZX9dctDUNpY8Y7 PACT project is Implemented by: Academy of Fine Arts of Naples, Action Synergy, Trakų rajono veiklaus jaunimo asociacija, Universidad de Sevilla, Young Agents of Change, Georgian Youth Development Association, "MilleniuM" Training and Development Institute, and Youth Development Center of Armenia. Co-funded by the European Union. Questions: info@yac.org.ua
audience: Armenia, Georgia, Greece, Italy, Lithuania, Moldova, Spain, Ukraine

publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: Digital Content & Pedagogical Practices
summary_en: Through practical activities, participants will explore two perspectives: how AI can support learning, and how it can help youth workers create and adapt content, plan activities, manage administrative tasks, and monitor and evaluate learning. Throughout the course, we will ask a central question: Where does AI add real educational value—and where does it not? The course also creates space for an open discussion of ethical concerns, data protection and GDPR, bias, authenticity, over-reliance on technology and the digital divide. Participants will put their learning into practice by building a learning programme step by step with the support of AI, from objectives and activities through to evaluation. Learning outcomes By the end of the course, participants will be able to: Identify digital content, AI and automation tools relevant to youth work and non-formal education. Use AI to support activity planning, administrative work, and monitoring and evaluation. Profile of participants: ✔Aged over 18 years old ✔youth worker representing an NGO active either in E+ or ESC programme , youth project manager, youth coaches ✔Fluent in English ✔Able to disseminate the results of the TC in social media and through their work ✔Be open-minded, motivated and ready to share experience and good energy

title: Wellness Navigators - Webinar Series
summary_en: Wellness Navigators Webinar Series Wellness Navigators is a series of six free online webinars created for youth workers, educators, trainers, facilitators, and anyone interested in supporting the emotional and social well-being of young people. Running from September 2026 to February 2027, the series explores practical approaches to well-being through the four dimensions of the Wellness Compass: Body, Mind, Emotions, and Connection. Each webinar combines accessible theory with practical tools, reflection, and experiential activities that can be used both for personal development and in educational work with young people. Topics include emotional awareness and regulation, connection and empathy, body-based practices, play and joy, and everyday strategies for strengthening resilience and well-being. The webinars are part of the Wellness Navigators Erasmus+ project, which develops practical educational resources to help young people better recognise their needs, understand their emotional and bodily signals, build healthier relationships, and navigate everyday challenges with greater awareness and choice. What to expect Participants will: discover practical tools for supporting youth well-being; explore the connection between body, thoughts, emotions, and relationships; learn experiential activities that can be adapted to youth work and non-formal education; gain inspiration from approaches such as Nonviolent Communication, embodiment, mindfulness, creative methods, and emotional education; receive access to webinar recordings and additional project resources. The webinars are free of charge and open to an international audience. Participants can register once for the whole six-part series and receive information and access links before each session. The webinar series accompanies the development of the Wellness Navigators toolkit and card deck, offering an opportunity to explore some of the ideas and practices behind the resources in greater depth. title: "European Network for Mental Health of Youth" Partnership Building Activity
summary_en: Join the European Network for Mental Health of Youth in Warsaw! Young people’s mental health and well-being are becoming increasingly urgent challenges across Europe. Many organisations are already responding through youth work, education, community initiatives and international projects. Now it is time to bring these experiences together, learn from one another and explore what we can create through European cooperation. The Q Zmianom Association invites youth workers and NGO representatives to take part in the European Network for Mental Health of Youth, a Partnership Building Activity taking place in Warsaw, Poland, from 21 to 29 November 2026. Connect, share and create The meeting will bring together people and organisations working with or for young people across Europe. During seven days of educational activities, participants will: meet inspiring organisations and potential international partners; exchange methods, experiences and good practices; discover local youth work and mental health initiatives in Warsaw; discuss the challenges currently affecting young people; explore self-care, nature-based regeneration and burnout prevention; learn about funding opportunities, including the Erasmus+ Programme; develop concrete ideas for future international projects; become part of a growing European network committed to young people’s well-being. The programme will combine workshops, study visits, networking sessions, outdoor activities, an interactive city game and project development in international teams. Who can apply? We are looking for participants aged 18 or above who: work with or for young people in an NGO based in an EU Member State or a third country associated with the Erasmus+ Programme; are interested in young people’s well-being, development and mental health; would like to exchange good practices and build long-term international partnerships; hold a decision-making role in their organisation or can actively contribute to developing new projects; c

publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: “GreenComp in Action – Sustainability Skills for Youth Work and the Labour Market”
summary_en: The programme is based on GreenComp – the European Sustainability Competence Framework, which supports the development of the knowledge, skills and attitudes needed to live, work and act sustainably. During the seven-day training course in Barcelona, participants will follow an intensive programme combining interactive workshops, non-formal education methods, experiential learning, practical exercises, teamwork, peer exchange and structured reflection. Participants will explore GreenComp's four interconnected competence areas: embodying sustainability values, embracing complexity in sustainability, envisioning sustainable futures and acting for sustainability. They will work with the framework's 12 competences, including systems thinking, critical thinking, problem framing, futures literacy, adaptability, collective action and individual initiative. The training course is developed in line with Youth Goal 8: Quality Learning, and contributes to: Ensuring young people have access to high-quality, relevant non-formal learning experiences that develop key competences for life, active citizenship and work. Promoting innovative, competence-based learning approaches that help youth work and education systems respond to the demands of the green transition and the changing labour market. A particular focus will be placed on connecting sustainability competences with employability, entrepreneurship, professional development and the future of work. Participants will examine how the green transition is transforming organisations, professions and workplaces and how GreenComp competences can help young people respond to these changes and recognise new professional opportunities. Youth workers will gain practical methods for translating GreenComp into engaging non-formal education activities. Through simulations, role plays, real-world case studies, group challenges and project-based learning, they will strengthen their ability to support young people in developing sustainability

publishing_authority_code: SALTO Resource Centre
title: Advocacy and Lobbying for international youth work
summary_en: The activity consist of 4 online workshops with first on 17th November, a residential seminar 15-20 March 2027 in Moldova and a final online meet-up in the middle of April. More details below. Apply ONLY if you can fully participate in all these elements! OBJECTIVES To map the advocacy landscape — Identify the Erasmus+ Youth actions, strategies and policies where programme–partner country cooperation should be advocated, the key decision-makers to target, and the data sources needed to support the case. To build advocacy and leadership competences — Develop participants' advocacy and lobbying skills, introduce effective methods and tools, and strengthen their leadership and communication capacity to use them. To position youth organisations as policy stakeholders — Raise awareness among youth organisations of their role in shaping policy in international youth work, and their potential to feed into future advocacy structures. EXPECTED PARTICIPANTS 25 representatives of youth organisations well experienced in cooperation between the programme and the partner countries (approx. 10 from programme countries and 5 per each of the 3 neighbouring regions); Personal experience as coordinator of at least 3 youth projects within Erasmus+ and European Solidarity Corps including programme and partner countries (coordination of the cross-regional projects, involving more than 1 partner region will be a strong asset) since 2020; Representing a youth organisation with the record of at least 6 youth projects within Erasmus+ and European Solidarity Corps including programme and partner countries since 2013; Able to work meaningfully in English; At least 18 years old; Committed to participate fully in all activities of the course. OBLIGATORY ELEMENTS OF THE TRAINING COURSE (the organisers keep the right to substitute a participant in case of absence in these activities): Tuesday, 17th of November 2026, 11.00 - 13.00 CET - Intro on concepts and getting to know each other Tuesday, 15th

publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: PBA Partners UP!
summary_en: Partners Up! is a Partnership Building Activity for representatives of European organisations that are ready to actively develop, write and submit new international cooperation projects. With a particular focus on Erasmus+ Small-scale Partnerships (KA210), Cooperation Partnerships (KA220) and other relevant European funding opportunities, Partners Up! is designed as a practical working space where organisations can find the right partners, build project consortia and transform shared ideas into concrete project concepts. From partnership to project concept Partners Up! goes beyond networking. Our plan is to bring together 25 participants representing around 20 different European organisations, creating a diverse pool of organisational experience, expertise, target groups and project ideas. During the PBA, participants will present their organisations and their potential for international cooperation, identify common needs and interests, form project consortia and work together on the framework of future European projects. Each participant will have the opportunity to work on at least two different project concepts within international consortia. The working process will focus on developing the foundations of each project, including: - needs and challenges to be addressed; -target groups; -project objectives; -partnership and consortium; -roles and contributions of partner organisations; -key activities and working methods; -expected results and impact; -sustainability and follow-up; -next steps towards project development and submission. The aim is not necessarily to complete an application during the PBA, but to leave with a clear project framework, a strong consortium and a concrete project concept that can be further developed towards submission. Who are we looking for? Partners Up! is primarily designed for representatives of organisations that are ready to develop, write and submit European cooperation projects. publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: LIMITLESS Training Course
summary_en: This training is designed for NGO leaders, entrepreneurs, and changemakers navigating uncertainty. Anyone ready to lead differently. The world is shifting in ways none of us have experienced before. Funding disappears. Rules change. People leave. And the old way of leading – pushing through, staying busy, carrying it all – doesn't work anymore. We’re offering 7 days to learn how to lead in a new way while staying true to yourself. This training is for you, if: You're wearing too many hats. Project coordinator, grant writer, team motivator, problem-solver – sometimes all in the same day. There's no one else to do it, so you do it all. You're stuck in reactive mode: firefighting every day while funding is uncertain, rules keep changing, and partners disappear. No time to think strategically, just trying to keep things from falling apart. You're exhausted. You wake up tired. You go to bed overwhelmed. You're on the edge of burnout, or maybe you've already been there. You're losing the fire. You started this work because you cared deeply. But now you're so exhausted and overwhelmed that you've lost touch with why you started. WE WOULD LOVE TO HAVE YOU IN OUR PROGRAM IF: You’re 18+ years old You reside in one of the Erasmus+ Programme countries You're running an NGO, part of the core team of an NGO, or a social entrepreneur working on impact-driven projects You're facing real challenges in your work – even if you can't name just one. We're looking for participants who want to solve real problems, not just explore out of curiosity You can commit to participating for the full duration of the program (November 11-17) You’re comfortable communicating in English. All the details in the infopack! Apply here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1G-EaXXvDC2z386QmQIwXeFqREaR2nGq-/view?usp=sharing

publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: Youth Work Off Autopilot
summary_en: Context In the first year of our accreditation, "The Outdoor Youth Work" taught us to use outdoor spaces for non-formal learning. Even outside, we met the same obstacle: attention. In discussions with partners during 2026, youth workers named three difficulties: agreeing on phone use without conflict, bringing a distracted group back to an activity, and responding when young people rely on AI for advice. In the wider context, problematic social media use among adolescents rose from 7% (2018) to 11% (2022) across 44 countries (WHO/HBSC, 2024), and 63.8% of 16-24-year-olds in the EU used generative AI tools in 2025 (Eurostat, 2026). AI gives rapid responses. It can support learning, and it may also encourage distraction, reliance on quick answers or less independent thinking. These effects differ between people and tasks, so youth workers need to observe them in themselves first. The outdoors is our deliberate low-tech contrast: away from notifications and feeds, participants can notice their own habits. Goal To enable youth workers to understand how using AI affects their own attention, critical thinking, confidence and decision-making, and to facilitate activities that help young people stay attentive and make intentional choices about technology. Objectives O1. To increase the self-awareness of 20 youth workers (volunteers, aspiring and active practitioners) regarding how AI use affects their own attention, critical thinking, confidence and decision-making, so that each can distinguish situations where AI supports learning from those where it hinders it. O2. To strengthen the competence of the 20 youth workers to facilitate inclusive, well-debriefed activities on attention and to make reasoned decisions on whether AI serves an activity's learning purpose. O3. summary_en: Come and discover in this beginner's course how you can organise volunteering activities for inclusion in the European Solidarity Corps. Discover the potential of volunteering projects for inclusion In 3 training days, we show you the possibilities that volunteering (within the European Solidarity Corps) has to offer for young people from disadvantaged or underprivileged backgrounds. A volunteering project might just be the life-changing opportunity for the disadvantaged young people you are working with: e.g. those from minority backgrounds, with access needs, with socio-economic difficulties, discriminated groups, in difficult situations, with limited opportunities, geographical disadvantage, health issues… Why participate? Volunteering is a rewarding methodology to reach your organisation’s inclusion aims. Come and experience the benefits that international cooperation can have for your organisation and young people with fewer opportunities. Explore the funding possibilities of the European Solidarity Corps and specific inclusion support. Learn to design a volunteering project step-by-step (sending or hosting, individual or in group, international or in-country). Discover the various resources available for volunteering and inclusion. Get inspired by local examples and fellow participants. At the end of the course, you will be ready to start organising a volunteering project with/by/for the young people with fewer opportunities with your organisation - sending or hosting. Who is the course for? This course is for NEWCOMERS to European Solidarity Corps (e.g. youth workers, social workers...) who are directly working with young people from disadvantaged backgrounds (e.g. facing social, economic, educational, geographic, cultural, health & disability challenges) If you NEVER organised volunteering activities in the European Solidarity Corps with the young people with fewer opportunities whom you are working with and would like to know what is possible, then this cou

title: 2nd Winter Youth Work Academy
summary_en: The activity is offered only to participants connected/working with organisations from the Erasmus+ Programme. Together, we will reflect on the work Europe4Youth has carried out over the past few years, explore its diverse applications, and inspire one another to strengthen good practices across different areas of youth work. Also, there will be a space to share experiences and observations from other known Erasmus+ activities. We want to achieve: • To deepen our understanding of youth work by exploring diverse topics, perspectives and relevant publications • To exchange experiences and reflect on our youth work practice and observations from the past year • To share practical methods, tools and good practices for working effectively with young people.

title: Training Course “Youth Exchanges for Youth ” 5th Edition - YOU for YOU 5
summary_en: “Youth Exchanges for Youth 5” (YOU4YOU5) is the fifth edition of a training course for people who discovered Erasmus+ KA1 and started wondering, “What if I could create this experience for young people?” If you participated in a Youth Exchange or Training Course, it may have changed something in you. Maybe it gave you new perspectives, new friendships, or simply made you think, "I want to do more than participate." YOU4YOU5 is about taking that next step. During the training, we will explore how a Youth Exchange goes from an idea to a real Erasmus+ project: identifying needs, setting objectives, designing meaningful learning experiences, creating impact, communicating, evaluating and managing a KA152-YOU project.

publishing_authority_code: National Agency
title: The Power of Non-Formal Education 2026
summary_en: Main aim To improve our educational impacts through experiencing a non-formal educational (NFE) process Why this Training Course? To stimulate the participants to feel and reflect about the power of non-formal education (NFE) by experiencing different educational methods. To broaden our perception of NFE and its potential impacts in our different realities in Europe. To explore the complementarity between formal and non-formal educational sector. To affirm the political dimension of non-formal education, as a way to take an active role in society (empowerment process). To reconsider our daily educational work practices, identify our challenges in order to improve the coherence between values we promote and our daily actions. How it will be done? In order to have real impacts, the participants experience an innovative approach, using a full immersion in the experiential learning cycle: doing/ feeling, reflecting, transferring... The TC is not limited to the five days the participants spend together but starts before the actual encounter. Participants should therefore be well aware that they will be actively involved from the very beginning. Besides the planned objectives and content of the activity, in informal moments, it is also an ideal opportunity to eventually find partners for future European projects. A fundamental flow during the training Experiencing: different educational settings, different methods (role play, simulation activity, exercises...). Reflecting: on the methods and its impacts, on the power and limits of NFE, on building a pedagogical process… Transferring: to the own reality of participants, in order to improve ways of working with young people. Sharing: different perceptions, current situations and experiences. Developing: the building capacity of the participants, by including them in the decision process of the project designing (participants will decide some sessions they feel they need to have) but also in the implementation of the program

title: Volunteering 360
summary_en: Here is the infopack with all information: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ea08s0Rn5ORX3mj3TXICWxXG9aJZ6_EL/view?usp=drive_link The project brings together youth workers and volunteer coordinators who are responsible for planning, coordinating and supporting volunteering programmes. With the project we aim to design, manage and evaluate volunteering programmes in a more structured, sustainable and inclusive way. Through two international study visits, participants will develop competences related to the entire volunteer journey - recruitment, onboarding, mentoring, learning support, participation, inclusion and long-term engagement. The project provides a space for self-reflection, co-creation, and practical application of methods that can be transferred to local realities. In doing so, it also promotes intercultural learning, solidarity among youth workers and the professionalisation of volunteering programmes. The programme is based on a non-formal education, with a strong emphasis on experiential learning, peer exchange, and learning-by-doing. Throughout the project, participants are encouraged to take an active role in shaping the content, contributing their experiences, questions, and ideas. The learning process is facilitated, but not imposed - we value reflection, collaboration and diversity of perspectives. The project is designed not only as a skill-building initiative, but as a supportive and caring learning space - one that recognises the emotional and social dimensions of youth work and volunteering programmes.
audience: Greece, Italy, Latvia, Slovenia

publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: “Emotional intelligence in Action” -from individual empowerment to collective wellbeing-
summary_en: The overall goal of this training course is to provide youth workers with an opportunity to explore and deepen their understanding of emotional intelligence and its vital role in fostering both individual and collective resilience. Resilience is not about coping alone—it grows through emotional intelligence, relationships, participation and belonging. In times of uncertainty, crisis, and prolonged stress, many young people (as well as adults), develop misconceptions about mental strength. They may believe that suppressing emotions, hiding vulnerability, or coping with everything alone are signs of resilience. Research and life experience consistently show the opposite. Genuine resilience starts within supportive relationships and is built through emotional awareness, healthy self-management, sense of belonging and contribution to something meaningful. Through experiential social and emotional learning (SEL), delivered in synergy with the principles of non-formal education, participants will not only develop these competencies themselves but also experience their practical value in their daily work with young people. The training can be especially valuable for those working with marginalized youth population. The course will further explore how meaningful participation, collaboration and community engagement contribute to individual wellbeing, confidence, and resilience. By strengthening their own emotional intelligence, participants will become better equipped to create safe and empowering environments, build trusting relationships with young people, and support them in developing resilience and becoming active, engaged members of their communities. The training course is developed in line with Youth Goal 5: Mental Health & Wellbeing, and contributes to the promotion of wellbeing and healthy living habits by: Encouraging the development of self-awareness and less competitive mindsets by fostering appreciation for individual skills and strengths. publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: Humour is Serious Business
summary_en: Humour is already present in youth work practice - but it's rarely used as a deliberate, structured tool. "Humour is Serious Business" (HiSB) is a 6-day Erasmus+ KA153-YOU training course (27 November - 3 December 2026, Hollókő, Hungary) that will help you turn something you probably already do instinctively into an intentional, ethical, and effective competence for engaging young people. This training is aimed specifically at practitioners in the field of non-formal learning and youth work - not at the general public. You should apply if you are a youth worker (professional or voluntary), a youth leader, a young person (18+) with leadership potential already identified by your organisation, or a practitioner with relevant expertise who works with young people (e.g. a coach, mentor or tutor), even if youth work is not your primary profession. Through non-formal methods - World Café, simulations and role play, clowning and improvisation, team building, and daily reflection groups - you will explore the many different types of humour, examine cultural differences in how humour is used, reflect on your own sense of humour, and develop concrete post-programme actions to bring back to your own community. Every participant leaves with a Personal Development Plan and the chance to earn a Youthpass. HiSB is delivered by an experienced international Training Team and hosted by MAVISZ (Hungary), together with partner organisations in Poland, Portugal, Armenia, Serbia, Latvia, Croatia, Montenegro and Spain. 36 participants will take part, 4 per sending country. Full details, including the daily programme, participant support structure, and reimbursement process, are in the Info Pack: https://mavisz.my.canva.site/hisb2026
audience: Armenia, Croatia, Hungary, Latvia, Montenegro, Poland, Portugal, Serbia, Spain

publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: E-motion: a practical guide to Emotional Intelligence in youth work!
summary_en: Across Europe and Neighbouring countries, youth work is increasingly shaped by complex emotional, social and psychological realities. Young people are navigating uncertainty, rapid social change, digital pressure, polarization and declining motivation in education, while youth workers are expected to respond with empathy, stability and inclusive support to these situations. Alongside emotional distress, many youth workers report growing levels of low motivation, disengagement, apathy and lack of initiative among young people, which directly affects participation in learning, community life and democratic processes. However, the emotional demands placed on youth workers are rising faster than the availability of structured training that equips them to manage emotions, both their own and those of the young people they work with, in a healthy, professional and sustainable way. In this context, emotional intelligence is no longer an optional “soft skill,” but a core competence for high-quality youth work, wellbeing promotion, motivation, participation and democratic engagement. "E-motion: A Practical Guide to Emotional Intelligence in Youth Work" training course is designed to respond to this gap by strengthening youth workers’ emotional intelligence as a key professional competence. While youth work is fundamentally based on human relationships, emotional intelligence competences such as self-awareness, emotional regulation, empathy, motivation and constructive communication are often insufficiently addressed within existing non-formal education training pathways. Youth workers frequently lack practical tools to respond to emotional withdrawal, low self-confidence, reduced intrinsic motivation and fear of failure, especially among young people with fewer opportunities. publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: S.A.F.E. Moves
summary_en: “Safe Moves” is an Erasmus+ project that strengthens the capacity of youth organisations to offer inclusive, safer, braver and high-quality learning experiences in international group mobilities like Youth Exchanges and ESC Volunteering Teams. It focuses especially on supporting young people with fewer opportunities and highly vulnerable youth. Over 7 days, participants will: understand safeguarding and risk management principles in short-term mobilities; explore the personal struggles young people may face abroad (homesickness, communication and language barriers, overwhelm, exclusion) and how to support them; practice first response to distress, conflict resolution and trauma-informed approaches; exchange practices and co-create the Safe Moves Toolkit on Safeguarding in International Youth Mobilities; reflect on competences through Youthpass and the YOCOMO self-assessment. Methods: non-formal education, including simulations, role-plays, case studies, discussions, creative activities and daily reflection groups. The Training Course builds on the results of the project's Study Visit. There, staff from partner organisations observed safeguarding practices in an ESC Team with highly vulnerable young people.
audience: Erasmus+ Youth Programme countries

Vegetarian options are prioritised, and dietary needs can be indicated in the registration form. In the spirit of the project, participants will take part in rotating cleaning groups.

publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: Connected Youth Work: From Non-Formal to Digital
summary_en: Connected Youth Work: From Non-Formal to Digital is an Erasmus+ international training course for youth workers, trainers, educators, facilitators, youth leaders and NGO representatives who are actively involved in non-formal learning and youth work. The activity is designed for people who want to strengthen their digital and methodological competences and learn how to combine non-formal education with modern digital tools. The programme will explore practical approaches such as storytelling, gamification, project-based learning, visual communication, multimedia creation and interactive online methods, together with the use of digital platforms and AI-supported tools. The training will focus on how digital tools can support, rather than replace, meaningful youth work. Participants will work on designing engaging, inclusive and participatory learning activities that can be used in face-to-face, online and hybrid settings. The course will be highly practical and based on non-formal education. Participants will learn through workshops, group work, peer learning, reflection, experimentation and hands-on creation of digital educational resources. They will also have the opportunity to exchange practices with colleagues from different European countries and develop materials that can later be adapted and used in their own organisations and local communities. The activity is particularly relevant for applicants who already work with young people in NGOs, youth organisations, community initiatives, educational projects or other non-formal learning environments and who are interested in improving the quality, inclusiveness and digital dimension of their youth work.
audience: Estonia, France, Greece, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Portugal, Slovak Republic

summary_en: Summary of the Project Learn more about us on IG What does democracy truly mean beyond casting a vote every four years? Is participation limited to the ballot box, or is it a daily practice of shaping public affairs with awareness, care, and intention? This project, Democracy Lab, invites youth workers, leaders, and active young people to explore democratic participation not merely as an institutional duty, but as a lived experience of community building, solidarity, and empathy. Set against the backdrop of the Spanish general elections happening concurrently during the training, we will use this unique timing to explore and deconstruct political culture, party systems, and electoral laws in Spain, comparing them critically with the realities and systems of other European countries. Together, we will reflect on how meaningful participation intersects with human rights and collective responsibility. Aim To empower 25 youth workers and youth leaders to foster meaningful and democratic participation in their local communities, expanding their understanding of democratic processes, human rights, and solidarity-based practices. To empower youth workers and youth leaders with practical tools, methodologies, and confidence to drive active participation in their local communities. summary_en: As autumn is unfolding in bright colors around us, as the world seems to grow more unpredictable, and the air becomes quieter, we can find ourselves turning inwards to listen to the quiet voice of our heart. What are you noticing? How are you harvesting old and new ideas? What ancient dormant powers are waking up inside of you, like autumn storms shaking the leaves? Are you feeling the call to bring people together? Perhaps explore together to find new ways of living, connecting with each other, or relating to the Earth? Have you wondered how to bring your idea to life and sustain this initiative, both socially and economically? Are you looking for inspiration and concrete tips and tools, and a touch of courage, so that you can take the next step when you’re ready? Re-Forage: a project for transformative action For the past two years, Andreea (cirkacph, DK) and Emmy (Relearn Suderbyn, SE) have explored collective empowerment through the Erasmus+ funded project called ‘Re-forage’. In the face of pressing environmental challenges, particularly among youth, the need for transformative action has never been more urgent. The main objective of Re-Forage was to empower youth(workers), to become catalysts for change in their own right. Through Re-Forage, we worked to equip young people with the knowledge, skills, and mindset necessary to navigate and address environmental challenges effectively, thereby creating a ripple effect for future generations. You’ll hear tips on what worked well (and what didn’t), advice on what to pay attention to for your (potential) future project, and receive inspiration on how to get started. The activity focuses on Education Through Sport (ETS) as a non-formal learning approach. Its aim is not to provide technical sport coaching, but to strengthen the quality of youth work by helping practitioners use sport and movement more intentionally as tools for learning, inclusion, participation and personal development. The PBA is especially relevant for participants who work directly with young people, including young people with disabilities and other young people with fewer opportunities, and who would like to develop more inclusive, accessible and educational sport-based activities. During the activity participants will: • get to know potential European partners and their youth work practices; • exchange concrete examples and good practices in Education Through Sport; • explore how sport activities can be adapted for mixed-ability and diverse groups; • discuss accessibility, safe participation, support needs and inclusion in youth work; • experience and analyse inclusive sport-based non-formal learning methods; • develop shared practical resources for youth workers and organisations; • identify opportunities for future Erasmus+ cooperation and develop realistic follow-up project ideas. title: Create with Makey Makey: Turning Everyday Objects into Interactive Learning
summary_en: Create with Makey Makey: From Curiosity to Creation through 5E and STEAM is an interactive e-learning training designed for youth workers, trainers, facilitators, educators and professionals who want to use creative technology as a tool for participation, experimentation and active learning. The training goes beyond learning how to use Makey Makey as a technical device. Its main focus is on how Makey Makey can be integrated into meaningful non-formal learning experiences by combining STEAM education, the 5E instructional model and interactive methodologies. Throughout the course, participants will experience the five stages of the 5E model: Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate and Evaluate. Each stage will be connected with practical Makey Makey activities and non-formal learning methods. Participants will begin with curiosity-based challenges and exploratory activities, investigating conductivity and discovering how everyday objects, water, fruit, aluminium foil, graphite, recycled materials and other conductive surfaces can become computer inputs. They will then explore how Makey Makey can be connected with Scratch and used to create interactive digital experiences such as sound installations, interactive posters, musical instruments, collaborative games, storytelling activities, art projects and team-building challenges. The STEAM approach will be embedded throughout the training: Science through conductivity, circuits and experimentation. Technology through Makey Makey and Scratch. Engineering through designing and testing interactive systems. Arts through music, storytelling, visual expression and creative design. Mathematics through sequencing, patterns, logic and problem-solving. The training is based on non-formal education principles and prioritises learning by doing, collaboration, experimentation, peer learning, reflection and active participation. publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: Inclusion in youth work- International training course on inclusive youth work
summary_en: Inclusion, with a focus on people with disabilities, is a key priority in youth work. However, creating truly inclusive events and activities often face practical and structural barriers. This training course addresses the critical need for disability-inclusive youth work. Across Europe, young people with disabilities continue to experience exclusion from social, educational, and recreational opportunities. Many youth organisations still lack the knowledge, skills, and resources to ensure full accessibility and meaningful participation for all. Youth workers, both voluntary and professional, play a vital role in advancing inclusion. By adopting inclusive practices, barriers can be removed and environments can be transformed to ensure that young people with disabilities are not only included but also empowered to participate fully. What it is about? International youth workers training course with around 25 people from Denmark, Finland, Estonia and Germany Opportunity to discuss the inclusion and participation of children and young people with disabilities in youth work Learn more about methods, tools, and opportunities for inclusion in youth work Workshops Excursions to Hamburg and in Schleswig-Holstein The opportunity to meet colleagues and multipliers from the Baltic Sea region Profile of participants Participants can be full-time or volunteer youth workers, multipliers or youth leaders from youth organizations who are interested in the topics. There is no age limit for this project. People with disabilities are very welcome, as their perspective is particularly important for this event! The project is funded by Erasmus+, the region of Schleswig-Holstein and Aktion Mensch. The participation is free of charge and travel costs will be reimbursed according to Erasmus+ standards. Further information and the link to the registration can be found on: https://www.ljrsh.de/arbeitsbereiche/internationale-jugendarbeit/fachkraefteaustausch/inclusion-in-yout-work/
audience: Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Germany, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, Norway, Poland, Sweden

publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: Action for Inclusion. Applying Inclusive Tools in Youth Work
summary_en: About the Training Course What if creating a truly inclusive environment was less about complex theories and more about practical, everyday actions? Action for Inclusion is a training course focused on providing you with new strategies and resources to improve inclusiveness in youth work. Throughout the week, participants will explore the different variables that can become hidden barriers to participation and, most importantly, discover how to dismantle them. The main goal is not just to talk about diversity. It is to discover how to actively build safe spaces, support mental health and manage sensitive realities within our communities. The training will give participants the opportunity to practice these strategies and develop the confidence to address discrimination and incorporate inclusive tools directly into their own educational and youth work activities. What will you get from the Training? You will have the chance to: - Deepen your understanding of what really means to be inclusive in our daily lives. - Acquire practical resources to design and implement inclusive strategies in your working environment. - Create safe spaces with a transversal perspective of the people you’re working with. - Manage sensitive topics confidently within your organisations and communities. - Develop the trust and competences needed to identify and address the discrimination towards different groups. - Face the challenges related with mental health and other obstacles against inclusion in your youth work practices. - Create new international connections and opportunities for cooperation Two experienced facilitators The training will be delivered by Víctor Paterna and Santiago Gallego, two experienced trainers and workers from the NGO sector. They work together in Las Niñas del Tul organisation, bringing into the table experience in working with volunteers at a local and international level and with vulnerable people, including those who were in an emergency situation.
audience: Erasmus+ Youth Programme countries , Partner Countries Neighbouring the EU

title: NextGen Facilitators
summary_en: Overview Are you an aspiring youth worker ready to step up as a facilitator? Join our 7-day Erasmus+ training course designed to equip you with the essential skills, tools, and confidence to design engaging workshops, understand non-formal learning, and kickstart your project organizer journey. Through intensive days filled with practical methods, dynamic activities, and peer exchange, you will explore group dynamics, practice debriefing, and discover how to handle challenging moments in a group. Along the way, we will dive into modern digital tools and AI to support your preparation and project workflow in an effective yet responsible way. You will also get hands-on experience by designing and delivering your own workshop live, receiving feedback from peers and trainers. This training course connects hands-on facilitation to the wider Erasmus+ project lifecycle: from a single 90-minute session to a full international initiative. You will meet motivated peers from across Europe, build lasting partnerships, and realize that your age is not a barrier to becoming a recognized youth worker and facilitator. What You Will Learn Gain insights into creating impactful workshops, particularly within the framework of non-formal education and the Erasmus+ programme. Learn how individual workshops scale into full international youth projects and understand the essentials of project design and project writing. Use digital tools and AI responsibly to boost quality and work more efficiently while learning about potential pitfalls. Develop confidence and practical facilitation competences through live workshop delivery, instruction-giving, and structured debriefing. Build an international network of emerging youth workers from 12 European countries to develop future high-quality Erasmus+ projects together. Who Can Apply We are looking for 24 participants from Portugal, Romania, Spain, Greece, Poland, Hungary, Croatia, North Macedonia, the Czech Republic, Italy, Austria, and Estonia.

summary_en: Disclaimer! The recrutation is ongoing, we will notify you about results up to date till 29th of October. Target Group The project is targeted at youth workers and educators actively using non-formal education methodology in their area of interest and/or work. The age group of participants is 20 to 30 years old. Run down During the 6 learning days of project, participants will: Learn and practice methods and skills useful in the mentoring process, such as setting goals, self reflection, learning through challenges, evaluation and feedback collection. Get basic knowledge of PFA (Psychological first aid), how it differs from other forms of psychological help and why it can be useful in the mentoring process. Simulate mutual mentoring processes and gather feedback from experience. Create a mentoring guidebook which can be used in the future as gathering of baseline knowledge and steps useful for mentoring young people. Methodology of training The project will be conducted with the use of non-formal learning practices. Trainers will provide meritorical content about the structure of the mentoring process, psychological first aid, evaluation models etc., but the emphasis will be put on learning from participants' experiences and conducting simulations. It is located in the Lubelskie Voivodeship, south-east of Warsaw. publishing_authority_code: National Agency
title: DISCOVERING YOU! - Empowering youth with fewer opportunities through DiscoverEU Inclusion projects
summary_en: The Erasmus+ Programme recognizes the diverse challenges faced by young people with fewer opportunities and implements dedicated measures to foster the inclusion of all young people. DiscoverEU Inclusion seeks to enhance its inclusion dimension by providing support to participants with fewer opportunities to explore Europe. DiscoverEU Inclusion offers young people who are between 18 and 21 years of age a chance to have a short-term individual or group experience travelling across Europe by rail. If you're eager to explore this topic further and tap into the opportunities offered by the DiscoverEU inclusion action, we invite organisations directly working with young people with fewer opportunities (aged 18 to 21) to apply for this training course. Don't miss this opportunity to make a meaningful impact on the lives of young people with fewer opportunities! MAIN GOAL The primary aim of the training course is to equip organisations with the skills and knowledge needed to plan, implement, and evaluate DiscoverEU Inclusion Action projects, ensuring the active involvement of youth with fewer opportunities. Specific objectives: - Introducing participants to the DiscoverEU Inclusion Action (its objectives, connection to the Erasmus+ priorities, quality criteria, and budget). - Providing participating organisations with the tools to successfully plan, prepare, implement, and evaluate DiscoverEU projects with an active role of young people with fewer opportunities. - Broadening understanding of young people with fewer opportunities, and obstacles they are facing in relation to opportunities/possibilities offered through DiscoverEU Inclusion Action, and to the European Strategy for Inclusion and Diversity. - Encouraging participants to reflect on European topics and values. The activity will take place in Turin, Italy, from 30th November to 4th December 2026 (3 activity days + 2 travel days). This training is open to 25 youth workers and representatives of youth organizations
audience: Erasmus+ Youth Programme countries

salto_specific.travel_reimbursement_text: Please contact your NA or relevant SALTO in order to know whether they would support your travel costs. If yes, after being selected, get in touch with your NA or SALTO again to learn more about the overall procedure to arrange the booking of your travel tickets and the reimbursement of your travel expenses.

publishing_authority_code: Others
title: Sustainable Project Management
summary_en: The Fifth DigiSkill Online Courses for Mastering Digital Project Management focused on Sustainable Project Management is on! This course will explore the principles and practices of sustainable project management. It will focus on integrating environmental, social, and economic considerations into project planning and execution. Participants will learn how to assess and manage the sustainability impacts of digital projects, including resource allocation, waste reduction, and energy efficiency. The course will also cover the frameworks and standards for sustainable project management, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Through practical exercises and case studies, participants will develop the skills to create and lead projects that contribute positively to sustainability goals while meeting their business objectives." �� Where: Online (Zoom link will be sent day before the activity) ��️ When: Every Thursday for 4 weeks at 13:00 CEST (November 5, 12, 19 and 26) ��‍�� Educator: �� Esmeal Sheriff Esmeal Sheriff is a project management professional, consultant and educator with extensive experience in project management, business development and professional skills training. As a PMP-certified professional, he brings practical, real-world experience into his training and mentorship. Every Thursday for 4 weeks, participants will join interactive 90-minute live sessions covering: Integration of environmental, social, and economic considerations into project planning and execution Management of the sustainability impacts of digital projects Frameworks and standards for sustainable project management, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. DigiSkill is an Erasmus+ initiative dedicated to bridging the digital gap in the youth and professional sectors. The project focuses on equipping young leaders and organizations with the essential digital competencies, innovative tools, and strategic mindsets required to thrive in a digital-first
audience: Erasmus+ Youth Programme countries , Other countries in the world , Partner Countries Neighbouring the EU

summary_en: We are pleased to invite key stakeholders, civil society representatives, and citizens from across Europe to participate in the online event entitled “Online Civic Awareness & Storytelling Campaign – Milestone Event”, organised by PYLON ONE within the framework of the project “CIRENA – Citizens Integration Initiative for a Reimagined and Reconstructed Solidarity-based Agenda in the European Policies they want” (Project No. 211164361). The event will take place online on 30 October 2026, from 13:00 to 15:30 CET, bringing together participants from different backgrounds to share experiences of solidarity, exchange perspectives on civic engagement, and explore practical ways to strengthen solidarity and social cohesion within European communities. Please note that all participants are required to complete both Zoom Registration and the Google Form, as both registrations are mandatory.

publishing_authority_code: National Agency
title: EuroPeers international Training Course 2026, Duisburg
summary_en: You took part in a volunteering activity, implemented a solidarity project or participated in a youth exchange, a youth participation project or another Erasmus+ youth or European Solidarity Corps activity? Probably you gained lots of experiences and got to know Europe from an exciting perspective. Are you interested in staying involved and sharing your experiences with others? If you can imagine telling other young people about your European experiences and encouraging them to try suchlike, we invite you warmly to become a EuroPeer! EuroPeers are young people who have already taken part in a European Solidarity Corps/Erasmus+ youth project. They share their experiences and inform other young people (their peers) about these opportunities and other ways to engage in society and go abroad. This can be done in different ways and in the framework of various events. During this international training course you will learn how to organise different types of EuroPeer events and how to share your European experience effectively with your peers. You will become part of a growing international network of active young people, meet other EuroPeers, get to know more about the European youth programmes and attend workshops on project planning and communicating the European idea. You will also have time to develop your first own EuroPeer activity. During a virtual follow-up meeting after the training course (date tbd) you will reconnect with the other participants and plan future events. At the end of the training you will receive a certificate. Curious now? Information about the EuroPeers project and previous events organised by EuroPeers over the last years can be found here: www.europeers.org and www.europeers.de/international The training course starts on Wednesday, 9 December 2026, with dinner (6 pm) and ends on Sunday, 13 December 2026, after lunch (around 1 pm).
audience: Austria, Belgium - DE, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Latvia, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Romania, Spain, Sweden

salto_specific.fee_text: This project is financed by the European Solidarity Corps Programme. Being selected for this course, all costs (accommodation, travel, visa, etc.) relevant to participation in the course will be covered by the NAs involved in this project - except a participation fee which varies from call to call and country to country. Please contact your National Agency to learn more about the financial details, and how to arrange the booking of your travel tickets and the reimbursement of your travel expenses.
salto_specific.accommodation_food_text: Unless specified otherwise, the hosting NA of this offer will organise the accommodation and covers the costs for accommodation and food.
salto_specific.travel_reimbursement_text: Please contact the National Agency in your country in order to know whether they would support your travel costs. If yes, after being selected, get in touch with your NA again to learn more about the overall procedure to arrange the booking of your travel tickets and the reimbursement of your travel expenses.

publishing_authority_code: National Agency
title: Mental health in youth work Training Course
summary_en: Youth Work Can Promote Mental Health The Mental Health in Youth Work training explores the role and competencies of the youth workers in supporting the mental health needs of young people by strengthening their emotional and mental health skills. Objectives The training course objectives are: Clarifying the understanding of what mental health means for ourselves Raising awareness of the importance of mental health in youth work Understanding the role of youth workers in promoting mental health in their work with young people Developing youth workers’ practical skills in supporting people’s mental health in their work Exploring approaches, tools, and resources that can be adapted in the organisation’s work Encouraging participants to reflect on their everyday practices with young people Enhancing the capacity to create a supportive, inclusive, and stigma-free environment Mental Health from a preventive perspective This training highlights mental health from a promotion and prevention perspective. In this training, we do not approach mental health from the point of view of diagnosis, therapy, or healing – these approaches belong to the professional work outside youth work practices. Time and venue The training will be hosted in Belgium; the exact location will be announced later. Monday, March 22 - arrival Tuesday-Thursday March 23-25 - working days Friday, March 26 - departure This training is organised under Mental Health in Youth Work long-term project
