publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: Key of Sustainability
summary_en: This Partnership Building Activity (PBA) brings together youth workers, NGO professionals and representatives of organisations active in youth work and non-formal learning who want to move from project ideas to strong, fundable proposals and sustainable international partnerships. The activity will take place in Vatra Dornei, Romania, from 12 to 17 January 2027 and will combine partnership building with hands-on project development and the strategic use of Artificial Intelligence in project writing. Rather than focusing on Erasmus+ KA1 mobility projects, participants will explore opportunities such as Erasmus+ KA2, relevant EU calls available through the Funding & Tenders Portal, and other European, national or local funding opportunities relevant to youth work and non-formal education. During the PBA, participants will work on real needs and project ideas, identify suitable funding opportunities, develop potential partnerships and explore how AI can support different stages of project development — from research and needs analysis to project design, intervention logic, drafting and critical review. The activity is designed as a practical working space, not only as a training course. Participants are therefore expected to actively contribute their organisational experience, ideas and expertise, while looking for potential partners with whom they can continue developing projects after the activity. The programme will use non-formal education, experiential learning, peer-to-peer exchange, practical workshops and collaborative project-writing sessions. The activity will be facilitated by Clotaire Ntienou, an experienced EU project director, grant writer, trainer and digital innovator with extensive experience in Erasmus+ and European project development. His work also includes the development and use of AI-based tools supporting NGOs in project design, grant writing and proposal evaluation. summary_en: UWC Spain is calling for applications for 60 openings a new edition of ActionxPeace, a bilingual English-Spanish programme to be held from December 4 to 8 2026, which invites young people born between 2009-2011 from diverse backgrounds to explore their role in peace-building and conflict transformation. title: EMPOWERING YOUTH WORKERS TO SHIELD AGAINST DIGITAL VIOLENCE
summary_en: e-SHIELD – Training Course on Digital Violence is a 5-day Erasmus+ training course designed for youth workers, youth leaders, educators, volunteers and other practitioners actively involved in youth work and non-formal learning. The training aims to strengthen participants’ capacity to recognise, prevent and respond to different forms of digital violence affecting young people, including cyberbullying, online harassment, hate speech, digital partner violence and emerging risks such as AI-generated harassment, deepfakes and violence in virtual environments. The programme is based primarily on non-formal education and experiential learning. Rather than relying on traditional lectures, participants will actively engage in role plays, case studies, simulations, forum theatre, group discussions, digital storytelling, practical exercises and intercultural teamwork. Expert inputs will be combined with opportunities to reflect on real situations encountered in youth work and to develop practical responses. A particular focus will be placed on equipping youth workers with methods and tools that can be directly transferred to their work with young people. Participants will explore how to facilitate activities on digital safety, recognise signs of online violence, support young people experiencing digital harassment and create engaging awareness activities and campaigns. The training will also provide an international learning environment where participants can exchange practices and experiences from different European contexts, work collaboratively and reflect on the gender and inclusion dimensions of digital violence. By the end of the course, participants will develop ideas for awareness activities, contribute to project tools and prepare an action plan for transferring their learning to their organisations and local communities. title: Green Games Lab: Innovating Youth Work Through Play
summary_en: The training aims to help youth workers make non-formal education more engaging, inclusive and effective through practical use of game design and gamification. Participants will learn how to turn educational goals into meaningful game-based activities that can be used with diverse groups of young people in youth clubs, schools, community centres and other youth-work settings. -Learn the basics of educational game design and build practical skills in creating games that support clear learning objectives. -learn how games can support topics such as human rights, civic participation, media literacy, anti-discrimination, environmental education, STEAM and soft skills. -Use gamification to increase motivation and engagement while keeping activities meaningful and connected to youth-work goals. -Create inclusive and accessible game-based activities that can be adapted to mixed-ability groups, different learning needs and young people with fewer opportunities. -Develop ready-to-use educational tools that participants can test, adapt and implement in their organisations and local youth-work practice. PARTICIPANTS This training course is suitable for: -youth workers; -educators; -trainers and facilitators; -NGO staff and volunteers; -people working directly with young people; -people working with young people with fewer opportunities; -people interested in game-based learning, educational games and gamification; -people looking for new practical methods to make youth work more engaging and participatory. publishing_authority_code: National Agency
title: Strengthening Mentoring in the European Solidarity Corps. Training of Trainers and Multipliers
summary_en: Quality mentoring rarely spreads by itself. It spreads through people who promote it into their training courses, their teams, their organisations and their networks. The Mentoring Competence Framework is a tool to raise the quality of mentoring support in volunteering projects. It provides clear and effective guidance for mentoring practitioners in the ESC Programme. Would you like to work with the framework in your own trainings and workshops? Would you like to support mentors to develop their mentoring practice? Would you like to encourage organisations in your national network to build and improve their mentoring support? If you want to refine quality mentoring, strategically or practically, we invite you to join “Strengthening Mentoring in European Solidarity Corps”, a training of trainers and multipliers built around the framework. This training course is designed for trainers, facilitators, mentors, tutors, project coordinators, project managers and members of National Agencies who are involved in European Solidarity Corps activities and would like to improve mentoring practices and mentoring support in the European Solidarity Corps Programme. During this training, you will get familiar with the Mentoring Competence Framework and prepare to work with it in your own context: as a TEC trainer or facilitator designing learning events, as a mentor or coordinator supporting volunteers, or as a National Agency working with TEC trainers and ESC organisations. Objectives Understanding the Mentoring Competence Framework Working with the framework and its assessment tools in practice Developing approaches and tools to improve mentoring with the framework in your context A special focus of the training will be on how you can integrate the framework into your own work: your training events, your national trainer pool, your mentors’ and tutors’ networks, and the support National Agencies offer to ESC organisations. At the end of the training, you will receive a Youthpass

title: OFF SCRIPT “ THROUGH AN EGYPTIAN LENS “ 20-24 November 2026 | Cairo, Egypt
summary_en: The training explores how digital media, photography, visual storytelling, and social media can be used as practical tools in youth work. Participants will learn how to transform ideas, youth activities, experiences, and social topics into engaging digital stories that can reach and inspire young people. Digital media has become one of the most powerful tools for communication, advocacy, education, and community engagement. Social media platforms allow individuals and organizations to reach diverse audiences, communicate complex ideas in accessible ways, and create campaigns that can influence attitudes and encourage meaningful action. However, effective digital communication requires more than simply posting content. It involves understanding audiences, developing clear messages, creating visually engaging content, using appropriate digital tools, and strategically planning campaigns. With the rapid growth of social media and digital communication, there is an increasing need to equip young people and future healthcare professionals with practical skills that enable them to communicate effectively in an increasingly digital environment. Despite the widespread use of platforms such as Instagram, TikTok, and other digital media, many young people have limited access to structured training in content creation, visual communication, photography, graphic design, storytelling, and digital campaign development. This creates a gap between consuming digital content and being able to intentionally create impactful and meaningful content. Goals & Objectives Equip participants with the basic knowledge and skills needed to plan and create effective social media content Develop participants’ practical skills in creating visually engaging digital content using accessible digital tools. Foster creativity, peer learning, and intercultural exchange among participants, enabling them to confidently apply their digital skills. Enable participants to integrate the digital communication

publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: FLY - FACILITATING LEARNING FOR YOUTH
summary_en: FLY – Facilitating Learning for Youth is a 9-day Erasmus+ training course for youth workers and facilitators, held 5–13 January 2027 at Küla Villa, Estonia, with 25 participants from 8 countries. Together we will design, facilitate and evaluate meaningful non-formal learning activities. Through hands-on X-Peeriments, peer feedback and reflection, you will build practical facilitation skills you can use in your own work straight away. All participants receive a Youthpass certificate, and we stay in touch after the course with follow-up activities in your own community. WHO CAN APPLY: Youth workers, trainers, facilitators, youth leaders and volunteers aged 18+ who work with young people. Participating countries: Estonia, Austria, Slovakia, Italy, North Macedonia, Romania, Slovenia and Türkiye. HOW TO APPLY Full programme, practical information and the application form are in the infopack. https://drive.google.com/file/d/1E46STR2Lrj-HX4hYIiUUvy7TmRQ_uOMm/view?usp=sharing Any questions? Write to marieta@eluksvalmis.ee
audience: Estonia, Italy, Republic of North Macedonia, Romania, Slovak Republic, Slovenia, Türkiye

salto_specific.accommodation_food_text: Accommodation and food are provided by the organisers at Küla Villa from 5 to 13 January 2027 at no cost to participants. Participants stay in shared rooms. If you want to arrive earlier or leave later, you can, but you need to organise and pay for your own accommodation and food outside these dates.
salto_specific.travel_reimbursement_text: Travel is covered by the Erasmus+ programme, up to the maximum per person for your country of departure: Estonia: up to €28 Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia: up to €309 Italy, North Macedonia, Türkiye: up to €395 Reimbursement is paid after the course, on presentation of tickets and proof of travel. Please do NOT book any tickets before your participation is confirmed and we have agreed your travel itinerary with you.

publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: Unlocking Learning: neuroeducation in youth work
summary_en: "Unlocking Learning: Neuro-education in youth work" is a founded Erasmus+ KA153 project, dedicated to youth workers with at least 6 months of experience. Newcomers to KA Erasmus+ events, or with limited experience are welcomed. The project aims to improve the competences of 30 youth workers, to be able to help young people to learn easier, be more impacted by what they learn and actually put that information into practise in this digital age, using neuroeducation, non-formal techniques. The total size of the group will be 33, including also 3 trainers. Selected participants will take part in Training Course mobility hosted in "Markutiskes, Vilnius, Lithuania" from 9th to 17th December 2026, and will also agree to contribute to local follow-up activities post-mobility. Applicants should be able to demonstrate their experience in youth work, providing 2 examples of their youth work activities in the last 6 months, and identify a possible future activity in which they could implement methodlogies learned during the training. Participation in the project is limited to applications from the following countries: Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, Romania, Bulgaria, Spain
audience: Bulgaria, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania, Spain

publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: Equal Ground Q1: Meaningful Participation — Beyond the Seat at the Table
summary_en: The European Network of Refugee, Migrant and Stateless Changemakers (ENRMSC) invites youth workers, youth leaders, trainers, community practitioners and other professionals working in non-formal learning and youth work to join the first session of Equal Ground, a quarterly ENRMSC dialogue series exploring meaningful participation, access to opportunities and accountability. About the session A seat at the table means little if the decisions are already made. Equal Ground Q1: Meaningful Participation — Beyond the Seat at the Table explores what meaningful participation looks like when refugees, migrants, stateless people and other communities are not simply invited into conversations, but have genuine opportunities to influence decisions, policies and actions. The session will examine the difference between being present and participating meaningfully. Who gets invited to the table? Who gets heard? Who gets to influence what happens next? Through a participatory, community-centred dialogue, participants will explore barriers to meaningful participation and consider how youth workers, organisations and institutions can create more effective pathways for people with lived experience to contribute to decision-making. What will participants explore? The session will explore: • Meaningful participation beyond consultation and representation • The difference between having a seat at the table and having influence • How lived experience can contribute to knowledge, leadership and decision-making • Barriers that can prevent refugees, migrants, stateless people and other communities from participating meaningfully • The role of youth workers and non-formal learning practitioners in creating inclusive participation • How organisations can listen to communities and translate their perspectives into action • How young people and community changemakers can move from participation to leadership • Practical approaches for creating more inclusive spaces for dialogue and decision-mak
audience: Erasmus+ Youth Programme countries , Other countries in the world , Partner Countries Neighbouring the EU

title: Global Solvers Accelerator_GSA_2027
summary_en: From challenge to progress: participants find inspiration and support to move forward The Global Solvers Accelerator (GSA) is for people already working on social, economic, and environmental challenges: grassroots activists, social entrepreneurs and intrapreneurs, SDG practitioners, action researchers, community organizers, and more. What matters isn’t a person’s title; it’s that they’re already running, co-leading, or actively shaping a project, and want to deepen both the work and themselves. With that in mind, well-suited candidates: * are between 20 and 35 years old; * are actively involved in an ongoing project, enterprise, research effort, movement, or community initiative tied to the SDGs – and can influence the decisions within it; * have a track record of real social impact; * want to connect globally, advance sustainable development, and help transform society; * are curious, open-minded, and forward-thinking team players who are at ease working with people from different cultures, backgrounds, and identities – online and in person; * bring a sharing mindset and a readiness to learn, unlearn, and relearn with peers worldwide; * have sufficient English language skills to take full part in every aspect of the program; * can commit roughly 4 hours per week to the program, including online engagement, regular meet-ups, and project-based assignments; * can attend the week-long Global Solvers Co-Lab (3–10 July 2027, in Germany, fully funded); * are eager to draw on the Melton Foundation’s global network to strengthen impact and practice global citizenship in local communities. Beyond the checklist, this program is for people who want to move past showcasing their project and dig into the questions beneath it; who let the process challenge and change them as much as they hope to challenge and change the world around them. It isn’t only about what participants have already achieved; it’s about the mindset they bring: participants show up consistently and authenti

salto_specific.city: Online GSA Program: 1st April – 30th November 2027. In-person Co-Lab: 3 – 10 July 2027
salto_specific.fee_text: At the Global Solvers Accelerator (GSA), everyone contributes – also financially. The program fee is 900 USD, which you will need to pay only if selected for the program. The 900 USD program fee also contributes to a dedicated fund that will support to the selected projects developed by participants after the program. Scholarships covering 20%, 50%, or 80% of the program fee are available to participants with proven need. If required, you must request a scholarship as part of your application form.
salto_specific.accommodation_food_text: Travel costs, accommodation, and meals in Germany are fully covered by the GSA.

publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: STAGE — Staging Tools for Awareness, Growth & Expression
summary_en: STAGE is an experiential training course for youth workers, youth leaders and trainers who want to bring body-based and theatre methods into their non-formal work with young people, with a focus on mental health, awareness and expression. You will explore four approaches: Gestalt Theatre, Spontaneous Movement, Río Abierto / Expressive Movement and Bioenergetics. You experience the methods first, then practise facilitating them with others. Movement, breathing, improvisation, reflection and group work are central to the learning process. Participation in each exercise is voluntary: you may step out at any moment without having to explain yourself. TWO MODULES — ONE LEARNING JOURNEY Attendance at both residential modules is required. • Module I: 28 February–7 March 2027, including arrival and departure; six working days, 1–6 March. Experience and explore the methods. • Between modules: facilitate at least two sessions with your own youth group, keep a short facilitation journal, and join three online supervision sessions of two hours each. Online dates will be agreed with the group. • Module II: 18–25 April 2027, including arrival and departure; six working days, 19–24 April. Develop your facilitation practice and integrate your learning. The calendar date range covers the whole programme; participants do not stay at the venue between modules. WHO SHOULD APPLY 25 places are available for participants from EU countries and Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia. The course is aimed at people actively working with young people in non-formal education who can put the methods into practice with their own youth group between modules and commit to the full programme. The working language is English. No previous experience of the body-based or theatre methods is required. STAGE develops youth work competences and does not qualify participants as therapists. VENUE AND LEARNING ENVIRONMENT Both modules take place at Albergue Casa del Trigo, La Almudema, near Caravaca de la Cruz, Murc
audience: Erasmus+ Youth Programme countries , Partner Countries Neighbouring the EU

salto_specific.city: Casa del Trigo, La Almudema, Caravaca de la Cruz (Murcia)
salto_specific.organiser_name: Red Europea Los Jóvenes Importan Ahora
salto_specific.fee_text: Participation fee: €150 per module (€300 for the complete two-module programme). The Erasmus+ funding allocated to STAGE supports five full training days per module. The team has decided to extend each module to six full training days, giving participants more time to practise, integrate the methods and receive feedback. The programme also includes supervision between modules, supporting participants as they apply the methods in their own work and prepare practical questions and experiences to explore during the second module. The participation contributions help cover the team’s work in delivering the two additional training days—one per module—and the supervision between modules, beyond the provision covered by the allocated grant. These contributions support fair remuneration for the additional work and are collected on a non-profit basis. Participants with fewer opportunities are exempt from the contribution. If the fee could prevent you from participating, please contact us confidentially so that we can address the barrier.
salto_specific.accommodation_food_text: Accommodation and all meals are covered by the project for both residential modules at Albergue Casa del Trigo. Participants stay in shared rooms of three with an en-suite bathroom. Training materials and working spaces are also provided. Please communicate dietary needs and allergies in advance. Bring your own towels.
salto_specific.travel_reimbursement_text: Travel is reimbursed separately for each module against original tickets, boarding passes and proof of payment, up to the applicable ceiling. Maximum amounts per module (standard / green travel): 100–499 km: EUR 161 / EUR 235. 500–1,999 km: EUR 259 / EUR 367. 2,000–2,999 km: EUR 345 / EUR 485. 3,000–3,999 km: EUR 530 / EUR 735. These project amounts already reflect a EUR 50 deduction for the organised private bus: return transfers between Murcia and the venue, plus transport to Águilas on the free day. Only actual eligible expenses are reimbursed. Before booking, contact the organisers to confirm the applicable budget for your place of departure, including any distance band not listed above. Green travel must be agreed in advance. Do not buy tickets until you receive written confirmation and booking instructions. Travel for both modules must be booked and confirmed by 20 January 2027.
salto_specific.venue_text: Casa del Trigo, La Almudema, Caravaca de la Cruz (Murcia), Spain

title: Democracy Reloading Webinars 2026: Developing youth participation in municipal decisions
summary_en: Democracy Reloading is organising four webinars in 2026. Each webinar focuses on one of the 4 key competences that ensure a more successful implementation of youth participation in municipal decision-making. You can read further details about the four focus topics below. Each webinar will be 90 minutes long and will include a presentation of practice of a local municipal youth policy officer and an introduction to one of the key tasks to be implemented for better success based on the Democracy Reloading approach. You can register for the webinars if you click on APPLY NOW. If you register, you will receive invitation to all four webinars in 2026. Three days before each webinar all the registered participants will receive an invitation email with the meeting link. Facilitators of the webinars: Carolina Loureiro (youth participation expert, Portugal) Dorka Vaczi (youth participation expert, Hungary) THE SPECIFIC TOPICS AND DATES: WEBINAR 1. The supportive municipality - 22nd April (Wednesday) between 15.00-16.30 CET Focus questions of this webinar: What are the benefits of engaging young people in municipal decisions? What are the typical doubts and how can you argue them? Who are the kep actors of a municipal authority that should support the idea? What are the initial conditions that the municipal authorty should provide before reaching out to young people? Guest speaker: Maja Björkebäck, Sustainability Strategist – Human Rights, Children's Rights, Public Health, Jönköping Municipality WEBINAR 2. Empowered young people - 20th May (Wednesday) between 15.00-16.30 CET Focus questions of this webinar: Where to find the right young people to be involved? How to ensure representativity and inclusion of less privileged youth? How to empower young people to be able to give their voice and influence municipal decisions? How to motivate them and keep them engaged? How to support them in their further carrier? Guest speaker: Zarina Dihal-Chedi, youth officer of Enschede, the N
audience: United Kingdom, Eastern Partnership countries , Erasmus+ Youth Programme countries , Southern Mediterranean countries , Western Balkan countries

title: TIC TAC - Training Course & Partnership Building Activity Mobility of Youth Workers
summary_en: 25-31 of January 2027 | Rome, Italy Bringing together youth workers representing youth organisations the TICTAC aims at improving the potential of the participants to get involved in the program and increase the quality of KA153 (Youth Worker Mobility projects). TICTAC is a network TC (training course) and PBA (partnership building activity) open for all programme countries of Erasmus+ (Youth) and European Solidarity Corps programme. It targets voluntary and professional youth workers and youth leaders involved in international youth work and interested in using the programmes as a tool in the strategic development of their work or organisation. By bringing together representatives of youth organisations from different European countries the TICTAC aims at improving the potential of the participants to get involved in the programme and consequently increase the quality of future international mobility of youth workers projects. TICTAC is built around long-term strategic planning and project cycle. TICTAC covers the main quality features of international youth work when building a local strategic plan as a tool for quality improvement of mobility of youth workers projects. TARGET GROUP The TICTAC is designed for youth workers and youth leaders, who ● have experienced an international activity before (not necessarily a project under the ERASMUS+ (Youth) or European Solidarity Corps programmes); ● are motivated to learn about and make use of the ERASMUS+ (Youth) programme for creating or strengthening international partnerships; ● are willing to work on the quality of their international projects; ● have the support of an organisation to attend the TICTAC and are in the position to implement European youth worker mobility projects in their organisation, ● are minimum 18 years old, ● are able to use English as a working language in order to establish effective communication during group-work and sessions. publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: The Playbook for Inclusion: Socio-Sports Leadership
summary_en: The Playbook for Inclusion is a training course focused on supporting young sports educators who want to use sport as a tool of social inclusion. It is also aimed for youth organisations that work with non-formal education for youth empowerment. The TC will serve to promote diversity in sports and increase awareness of gender equality. MAIN OBJECTIVE TO PROMOTE socio-sports ACTIVITIES in youth organizations and non-formal education, as instruments to promote social inclusion and youth empowerment. SPECIFIC OBJECTIVE To train participants with social skills and technical competencies to lead and design socio-sports activities for social inclusion and community building. To raise awareness and provide tools to participants about the need to promote physical and sports activities to train inclusivity from diversity, with special attention to gender equity. To establish networks of relationships, knowledge exchange and cooperation, between participants and their organizations, around sport as an inclusive and educational activity. publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: TC WINTER 27 - Adventure and Experiential Learning for Personal Growth & Wellbeing
summary_en: TC WINTER 27 – Adventure and Experiential Learning for Personal Growth & Wellbeing is an immersive training course for youth workers, trainers, facilitators and educators interested in exploring how adventure, nature and experiential learning can support personal development and wellbeing. The training is built around a simple principle: experience becomes learning when we create the space to reflect on it, give it meaning and connect it with our everyday life and professional practice. Throughout the programme, participants will be actively involved in outdoor activities, individual and group challenges, reflective practices and facilitated learning processes. The experiences will engage the physical, emotional, cognitive and relational dimensions of learning, inviting participants not only to learn new methods, but also to observe themselves within the learning process. The course will explore how adventure and experiential learning can help people develop greater self-awareness, confidence, resilience, emotional regulation, connection with others and a stronger sense of personal wellbeing. Participants will have the opportunity to: experience adventure and outdoor experiential learning first-hand; explore the relationship between experience, reflection and personal growth; develop greater awareness of their own resources, limits and learning patterns; understand how nature and adventure can contribute to wellbeing and meaningful learning; explore facilitation and reflective practices that help transform an experience into learning; exchange practices and perspectives with youth workers and educators from different European contexts; reflect on how these approaches can be transferred into their own work with young people. The methodology will be highly experiential and participatory. Rather than focusing mainly on lectures or theoretical inputs, participants will learn through direct experience, observation, reflection, dialogue and experimentation. The programme
audience: Austria, Cyprus, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Latvia, Netherlands, Portugal, Spain

salto_specific.accommodation_food_text: Accommodation, meals and programme activities during the training course are covered by the hosting organisation.
salto_specific.travel_reimbursement_text: Travel costs will be reimbursed up to a maximum of €309 per participant, based on the actual eligible travel expenses incurred. Participants are required to keep and submit all relevant travel documents and proof of payment, such as tickets, boarding passes, invoices and receipts. Only documented and eligible travel costs can be reimbursed. Travel reimbursement will be processed after the end of the training course, once: all required travel documents and proofs of expenditure have been submitted; participation in the full programme has been completed; the participant has completed the required Erasmus+ participation report/evaluation. Participants are therefore expected to initially purchase and cover their own travel arrangements. Any travel costs exceeding the maximum reimbursement amount of €309 per participant will be the responsibility of the participant.

publishing_authority_code: Others
title: Life in It Training Course
summary_en: Life in It is a two-part Erasmus+ media training for people active in youth work and non-formal learning, including youth workers, trainers, educators, volunteers, project coordinators and people involved in their organisation’s communication. No previous filmmaking experience is required; the focus is on learning through practice, collaboration and experimentation. The learning journey starts with online preparation and continues with Frame One in Germany (13–19 December 2026), where participants explore practical filmmaking, storytelling and media tools by working in international crews and creating content in real local contexts. Between the two international phases, participants bring the learning into their own organisation or community, including a small focus group with young people and further local practice. The journey continues with Frame Two at Hopeland, Greece (22–29 September 2027), where participants explore how the same storytelling foundations can be adapted to shorter, vertical video and social media formats. The methodology is strongly based on non-formal education and learning by doing: short inputs, practical assignments, teamwork, feedback, reflection and creative decision-making are at the centre of the programme. Life in It is designed as one learning journey rather than two separate trainings, with online preparation, two residential phases, local practice and follow-up. Priority is given to applicants who can take part in the complete process and use the learning afterwards in their youth work, organisation or local community.

publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: Move, Play, Create : Circus and Physical Theatre as Tools for Youth Work
summary_en: This training course introduces youth workers, educators and facilitators to circus and theatre as practical tools for youth work and non-formal education. No previous circus or theatre experience is required. Through hands-on activities, participants will discover the basics of juggling, partner and group acrobatics, clowning and physical theatre, while learning how to adapt these activities into accessible and meaningful workshops for young people. The course is based on circus pedagogy: an educational approach that uses circus not primarily to train performers, but to support personal and social development. Circus activities create opportunities to cooperate, communicate, build trust, take on challenges, be creative and experience success. Participants will explore how these activities can foster young people's confidence, creativity, cooperation, persistence, coordination and social connection. A key focus will be accessibility and inclusion, exploring how circus can be adapted to different ages, physical abilities, levels of experience and backgrounds. Participants will also discover how a group can move from individual games and activities towards creating a short collective performance. They will explore the pedagogical and practical aspects of the creative process, including generating ideas, sharing roles, connecting different disciplines and ensuring that everyone can contribute. By the end of the training, participants will have a practical repertoire of circus and theatre activities and greater confidence in using them in their youth work.

publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: ICT&SM 4.0: Advancing Digital Youth Work for Civic Engagement
summary_en: Project Summary: Leveraging ICT and Social Media for Youth Inclusion and Participation Aim of the Project: The project is designed to equip youth workers with digital skills and tools to strengthen civic participation and engage young people through Information and Communication Technology (ICT). A core aim is to promote civic engagement through digital tools. Objectives: Strengthen Digital Competencies: Provide practical training in ICT, social media engagement, and digital content creation. Youth workers will be trained to guide young people in critical media analysis, recognizing misinformation, and using digital platforms for youth activism and community participation. Ensure Inclusion and Equal Access: Develop strategies to engage marginalized and disadvantaged young people who face barriers to digital participation. Encourage Innovation: Introduce interactive, gamified, and blended learning approaches to make digital engagement more dynamic and adaptive. Strengthen Transnational Cooperation: Establish a European Digital Youth Work Network for collaboration and knowledge exchange, and develop a Digital Civic Engagement Toolkit with practical resources. Outcome: The project aims to significantly enhance the digital skills of youth workers and strengthen youth engagement through the use of digital tools for non-formal education and social participation. It seeks to expand civic participation through youth-led activism and make digital youth work more accessible and inclusive for young people from diverse and disadvantaged backgrounds. The project's sustainability will be ensured through the creation of a European-wide network of digital youth workers and an open-access toolkit, ensuring that the methodologies remain relevant and scalable.
audience: Cyprus, Czech Republic, Germany, Italy, Norway, Serbia

title: ENVIRONMENTAL LEADERSHIP
summary_en: This Erasmus training on Nature Leadership invites participants to discover new ways of leading inspired by nature. Through practical experiences, reflection, and teamwork, we will learn to connect with our environment and ourselves. We will explore skills such as listening, adaptability, and collaboration and leadership. It is an opportunity to develop a more conscious, sustainable, and human approach to leadership.Participants will develop leadership skills, share experiences, and learn from each other in order to create more inclusive, effective, and inspiring activities. They will: -Sleeping in a large share room in a hostel and sleeping one night outside in tents, and preparing some meals together, with participants taking part in the cooking process. -Simulating situations similar to those experienced during a Youth Exchange, developing leadership skills through practical learning. -Sharing best practices and learning from each other’s experiences. -Creating new partnerships and strengthening cooperation between organisations. Please enroll here: https://forms.gle/qUYa3mMH47aa8cSx7 If you have been selected we will have an online interview with you at last 31 December 2026.
audience: Erasmus+ Youth Programme countries , Partner Countries Neighbouring the EU

salto_specific.accommodation_food_text: We will organise and provide accommodation and meals throughout the training. Participants will stay in a youth hostel, sharing a large common room without gender separation. Some meals will be prepared together as part of the learning experience, encouraging teamwork, participation and exchange among participants.
salto_specific.travel_reimbursement_text: Participants will need to cover their own travel costs up to the maximum amount established for their country according to the Erasmus+ Programme Guide. After submitting all the required travel documents, such as receipts, tickets, and invoices, the eligible travel expenses will be reimbursed.

title: From Lived Experience to Opportunity, Knowledge and Action: European Dialogue & Capacity-Building Forum 2027
summary_en: The ENRMSC European Dialogue & Capacity-Building Forum 2027 will take place in Warsaw, Poland, in April 2027. The forum will bring together young refugees, migrants and stateless changemakers, youth workers, youth leaders, researchers, academics, civil society organisations, public institutions and other practitioners working with young people. The forum is built around a simple question: How can we move from young people being affected by systems to young people meaningfully shaping knowledge, opportunities, policies and solutions? The programme will explore meaningful participation, access to education and professional opportunities, community leadership, research and evidence, youth engagement, advocacy and collaboration between communities and institutions. Participants will take part in interactive discussions, panel sessions, workshops and facilitated group activities. The programme will combine knowledge exchange with practical capacity-building and opportunities for participants to develop new connections and potential European cooperation. A particular focus will be placed on recognising lived experience as expertise. Young refugees, migrants and stateless people will not only participate as beneficiaries but as contributors, knowledge holders, community leaders and partners in shaping discussions and recommendations. The forum will also connect participants with relevant European opportunities, networks and potential partners, including opportunities related to youth work, education, research, leadership and civic participation. The event is particularly relevant to people working in non-formal learning and youth work who engage with young people from refugee, migrant and stateless backgrounds. The guiding principle of the forum is: “Nothing About Us Without Us.” The forum is currently being developed by the European Network of Refugee, Migrant and Stateless Changemakers (ENRMSC), a refugee-, migrant- and stateless-led European civil society organisation.
audience: Erasmus+ Youth Programme countries , Other countries in the world , Partner Countries Neighbouring the EU

salto_specific.organiser_name: European Network of Refugee, Migrant and Stateless Changemakers (ENRMSC)
salto_specific.fee_text: Participation fees will be tiered according to participant category. Community participants and people facing financial barriers will have access to free or subsidised places. Indicative fees will range from €30 for students/early-career participants to €150 for institutional/professional participants. Fee waivers and sponsored places will be available.
salto_specific.accommodation_food_text: Accommodation is not provided by the organiser. Participants are responsible for arranging their own accommodation in Warsaw. Information on affordable accommodation options will be shared with selected/registered participants. Catering during the event will be provided where possible. Further details will be communicated to participants once the programme and venue arrangements are confirmed.
salto_specific.travel_reimbursement_text: Travel costs are not currently guaranteed to be reimbursed. Limited travel support or sponsored places may become available subject to funding and will be communicated to participants once confirmed.

publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: Heritage Revised — New Media Approaches to Heritage Awareness in Youth Work
summary_en: Why this programme? Young people increasingly experience the world through digital, visual, interactive and participatory media. At the same time, heritage education can sometimes remain centred on traditional formats: guided tours, exhibitions, historical information and passive observation. This creates an opportunity for youth work. New media can provide alternative entry points into heritage, allowing young people to: explore places and stories through immersive experiences; discover hidden or forgotten narratives; connect personal and community memories with wider European heritage; question dominant interpretations of history; create their own narratives; collaborate across cultures; transform physical spaces into interactive learning environments. The programme therefore does not aim to turn youth trainers into technology specialists. Instead, it aims to help them become creative facilitators who know when, why and how to use technology to create meaningful learning experiences. General aim To strengthen the capacity of youth trainers to use new media and emerging technologies as tools for heritage awareness, intercultural learning, creativity and youth participation. Specific objectives By the end of the training, participants will be able to: Explore contemporary approaches to cultural heritage and heritage awareness. Identify opportunities for using immersive and interactive media in youth work. Experiment with VR, AR, 360° media, projection mapping, interactive installations, digital storytelling and other creative technologies. Design non-formal education activities connecting young people with local, national and European heritage. Use storytelling and participatory methodologies to make heritage more relevant to young people. Encourage young people to question, reinterpret and remix heritage narratives. Develop low-cost and accessible digital heritage activities that can be replicated in different youth-work contexts. Create a prototype heritage-awaren

publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: Youth+: How to help youth with fewer/less opportunities grow in volunteering projects
summary_en: This course is a self-paced, interactive, practical course for Youth Workers to learn how to support groups of youth with fewer/less opportunities in creating and realizing their own volunteering projects and use it as an experiential learning process for the volunteers. It is a Beta version, please provide your feedback on the feedback forms incorparated into the course, to help us make it as good and useful as possible! You are going to learn about: - how to approach youth with fewer/less opportunities, - how to mobilize and recruit them to create their own volunteer projects, - how to work with them, - how to inspire, connect, empower, coach and mentor them in this process. About this course: In this course, you have a chance to learn about supporting youth with fewer/less opportunities who come from minority or socially disadvantaged background in the context of youth work. More specifically you can learn about how to support a group of youth with fewer/less opportunities in a non-formal learning program that is based on volunteering. The above-mentioned topics are explored by sharing and expanding a field-tested practice of working with Hungarian youth living in foster care and in segregated minority communities run since 2011. This method is called: From Us to You (FUY/FUYI - but we like to pronounce it FUJI). Aims and objectives of the course: The course aims to introduce the elements of the From Us to You program that make a volunteering based non-formal education program effective. By doing so we would like to share what we have found useful in our work in supporting youth with fewer/less opportunities. Besides our learnings, we also share the resources and approaches we have learned from within or outside of the field of youth work. More concretely, you will have a short glimpse into: - Experiential education - Solution focused approach - Trauma informed approach. publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: Ladder to Inclusion - Create Safer International Mobilities for Highly Vulnerable Young People Online Course
summary_en: How can international youth mobility become truly safe, inclusive, and empowering for Highly Vulnerable Young People? A course for youth workers, facilitators, and organisations to learn how to create safer, more inclusive, and trauma-informed international mobility experiences for Highly Vulnerable Young People (HVYP). This is a self-paced and practice-oriented online course for professionals working in youth mobility and non-formal education. The course supports participants in developing the competencies needed to responsibly include and support young people facing multiple and intersecting barriers in international programmes. You are going to learn about: safer and more inclusive mobility environments, safeguarding and risk management in practice, trauma-informed and solution-focused approaches, recognising and preventing harm and exclusion, supporting HVYP before, during, and after mobility experiences, professional boundaries, crisis response, and self-care in youth work. About this course International youth mobility projects can create powerful opportunities for learning, participation, connection, and personal growth. At the same time, for highly vulnerable young people, unfamiliar international environments may also involve increased vulnerability and risk. This course was developed within the LADDER project to support youth workers and organisations in creating mobility experiences that are not only accessible, but genuinely safe, supportive, and empowering. Through practical examples, case studies, reflection exercises, and field-tested approaches, participants will strengthen their capacity to: create safer and more inclusive mobility projects, anticipate and prevent risks, respond responsibly to challenging situations, and support young people facing multiple barriers. publishing_authority_code: Youth NGO
title: Connecting garden
summary_en: The project arises from a shared observation among young people, community development professionals, and partner organizations: a growing need to reconnect with the living world, rebuild social bonds, and collectively reflect on current ecological challenges in the face of the climate emergency. It addresses two main needs: Strengthening the skills of facilitators and community leaders so they can design and implement educational projects with strong social and ecological impact. Actively engaging young people in meaningful, concrete, and transformative projects. The project uses the living garden as an educational, sensory, and cooperative tool, helping to recreate connections between humans and ecosystems. These spaces become platforms for social transformation, civic education, and territorial resilience. It is based on active pedagogy that promotes autonomy, local engagement, and the transversal skills required for the ecological transition. The event will take place outdoors and is aimed at educators, activity leaders, and facilitators. In Brittany, 27 participants are expected.

title: REEL: Reflection, Expression, Empathy and Learning through Film
summary_en: The training aims to develop participants’ practical skills in using films and short films as tools for non-formal youth education and to teach them how to create learning spaces where young people can reflect, express themselves, develop empathy and learn through dialogue. During the course, participants will explore how films and short films can be used in youth work with groups of different levels, interests and needs. They will learn how to select films and scenes according to the objectives of a particular activity, the age and interests of young people, and their diverse needs. Participants will explore practical methods for facilitating discussions and reflection before, during and after a screening, connecting what young people watch with their own experiences and wider social issues. The course will also focus on creating safe spaces for discussing sensitive topics and on adapting screenings, discussions and creative tasks so that young people with different abilities and needs can participate fully. Participants will also learn how to design and test their own film-based activities for youth groups and explore how to create and develop youth film clubs as spaces for shared viewing, dialogue, reflection and interaction. The course provides an opportunity to explore tools of non-formal education, the Erasmus+ programme and international cooperation in youth work. The training is designed as a practical learning process that connects the use of film with concrete methods of non-formal education and approaches that participants can apply in their youth work. Objectives of the training: The main objective of the training is to develop participants’ competencies in using films and methods of non-formal education to create accessible and inclusive learning spaces where young people can reflect, express themselves, develop empathy and learn through dialogue. title: FIND YOUR PRESENT
summary_en: FIND YOUR PRESENT Erasmus+ Training Course for Youth Workers 12–21 November 2026 “Find Your Present” is an Erasmus+ mobility project for youth workers focused on emotional well-being, self-reflection and creative approaches to working with young people. The project was created in response to the growing need for youth workers to strengthen their emotional resilience, prevent burnout and develop practical tools for maintaining balance in both their personal and professional lives. During the training, participants will explore a wide range of creative, mindfulness, body-based, artistic and experiential practices that can be adapted to everyday youth work. Objectives and Topics The project explores creative and experiential approaches to emotional well-being, self-reflection and professional sustainability in youth work. The main objectives are to expand emotional well-being tools by exploring mindfulness, meditation, creative practices, performative arts and improvisational theatre; strengthen self-reflection and emotional resilience by developing awareness of emotions, personal boundaries, inner balance and burnout prevention; encourage creativity as a tool for self-expression, emotional self-regulation and personal development; introduce innovative methods that can be adapted and integrated into everyday youth work practice; support sustainable transfer by helping participants bring new methods into their organisations, activities and work with young people; and create opportunities for international cooperation through sharing experiences, methods and good practices with youth workers from different countries. Participant Profile Participants must be youth workers, educators, youth organisation representatives, active volunteers or other professionals actively working with young people. salto_specific.travel_reimbursement_text: Reimbursement applies only to flights, trains, and buses. Intercity bus tickets that do not include the participant’s name will not be reimbursed. Travel by car, cabs, or any other private means of transport is not eligible. You can arrive max two days before and leave max two days after the mobility. Arriving during the activities is not allowed. If you don't participate in at least 80% of the activities without a valid reason, there will be no reimbursement. Invoices from travel agencies will not be accepted. Please book your tickets directly on the websites of flight airlines, trains and buses. Reimbursement will be done in EUR. (according to the exchange rates from the official European Commission website via bank transfer after all your original documents are uploaded to the folder.
